title: Algebraic inverse image of ring and module sheaves
statement: Let $(C,J)$ and $(D,K)$ be small sites, $L:\operatorname{Sh}(C)\to\operatorname{Sh}(D)$ a functor on sheaves of sets, $R$ a sheaf of commutative rings on $C$, and $R_I$ a sheaf of commutative rings on $D$. An algebraic inverse-image presentation consists of an isomorphism $e_R:L(|R|)\cong |R_I|$, a functor $I:\operatorname{Mod}(R)\to\operatorname{Mod}(R_I)$ [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], and a natural isomorphism $e_M:|I(M)|\cong L(|M|)$, transporting ring addition, multiplication, zero and one and module addition, zero and scalar multiplication. More explicitly, for every test sheaf $T$ and arrows $a,b,t$ into the operand and result sheaves with the sectionwise equation $t=a+b$, $t=ab$ or $t=a\cdot b$, their images under $L$, identified by $e_R$ and $e_M^{-1}$, satisfy the same equation on every section over every object of $D$. Likewise every arrow identically zero or one remains so after transport. Additive inverses are determined by addition and zero. The natural isomorphism $e_M$ fixes the action on module morphisms. These graph conditions express transport along the inverse finite-product comparison; they determine the algebraic structures up to the stated identifications. The structure can be defined for an arbitrary $L$; finite-limit preservation is imposed when it presents inverse image of a morphism of topoi.
